evidence_judgment.instructions: What does `passage.text` establish about the statement in `control.statement` for the system and actions described? Judge only this passage, not other documents or legal compliance.

criteria.supported: The passage establishes the approval arrangement required by the control statement for the relevant system and actions. Generic human involvement alone is not sufficient.
criteria.contradicted: The passage explicitly describes an arrangement incompatible with the control statement, such as execution without the required approval. Silence about approval is not a contradiction.
criteria.insufficient_evidence: The passage does not address the required approval arrangement, or concerns a different process or review target, such as editorial review of release notes.
criteria.ambiguous: The passage addresses the relevant arrangement but its wording is vague, conditional, or internally conflicting, so neither support nor contradiction can be established.

addresses_control.instructions: Does `passage.text` address human approval or control of the relevant system actions in `control.statement`?

criteria.true: The passage discusses approval or control of the relevant actions, including absent, vague, or conflicting arrangements.
criteria.false: The passage describes unrelated activities or gives no information about approval or control of the relevant actions.

evidence_judgment.instructions: What does this exact passage establish about `control.statement`? Evaluate the system actions specified in that statement. Do not assume missing workflow steps, infer execution from leaving a queue, or judge legal compliance.

criteria.supported: The text establishes that a human approves every relevant recommendation before execution. Approval of training data, a manual, or another process is not approval of system recommendations.
criteria.contradicted: The text explicitly permits at least some relevant recommendations to execute without prior human approval. After-the-fact review alone does not meet prior approval.
criteria.insufficient_evidence: The text supplies no information about approval or control of the relevant deployed actions. Data formats, editorial checks, and training-data review alone are insufficient.
criteria.ambiguous: The relevant arrangement is mentioned but vague, has unresolved workflow timing or scope, or includes incompatible claims about the same deployment.

addresses_control.instructions: Does this exact passage help establish, dispute, or locate documentation of `control.statement` for this system?

criteria.true: It states an approval arrangement or its absence, gives a vague or conflicting human-control claim, or provides a relevant scope note, revision note, control alias, or source reference. A broken link is only a lead, not evidence of its missing contents.
criteria.false: It only shares topic words, describes data or outputs without control information, or concerns review of another target such as spelling, manuals, or training labels.

control.title: Human Oversight
control.statement: A human must approve every recommendation before the system executes it.

payload.design: One request per case per fixed configuration; no retries. Equal state, pinned model, predeclared 17 development / 12 held-out cases. No tuning after held-out predictions. Noul v1 addresses-control and v2 source-finding relevance have different semantics; they are not calibrated equivalents.

passage.text: A human supervisor must approve every recommendation before the Dispatch assistant executes it. The supervisor may reject a recommendation.
The assistant proposes delivery sequences from synthetic parcel records.
The Dispatch assistant executes every recommendation automatically without human approval. Operators cannot stop or override execution.
This runbook describes the same deployment covered by the Dispatch policy.
Humans remain in control of the Study tutor. Responsible use is important.
The tutor suggests practice exercises from fictional learning records.
The system converts fictional ledger entries into monthly summaries.
Summary tables are stored in a training workspace. The input schema contains amounts and dates.
A human editor reviews the spelling of release notes. This process does not review the Dispatch assistant's recommendations.
The notes describe changes to the demonstration software.
A staff member must countersign each proposal before it leaves the queue.
This procedure applies to the Dispatch assistant's proposed delivery sequences.
A designated staff member must countersign each proposed delivery sequence before the Dispatch assistant executes it.
This register calls Human Oversight the Two-person Gate control for the Dispatch assistant. The Gate rule and Related sources sections specify this local control.
The Dispatch assistant executes proposed delivery sequences without a countersignature. Staff authorization is not required.

See [Queue gate](evidence:dispatch-signoff@1#Queue%20procedure%20%2F%20Final%20gate), [Execution](evidence:dispatch-runbook@1#Dispatch%20runbook%20%2F%20Execution), [Historical gate](evidence:dispatch-gates@1#Dispatch%20gate%20register%20%2F%20Gate%20rule), and [Unpublished annex](evidence:unpublished-annex@1#Annex).
Revision 2 supersedes revision 1 of this register. It does not revise the queue procedure or resolve its scope.
